subject: Investigation: Coordinated multiple-account credit appeals / promotion abuse
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <ops@hyperledger.ai>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: multiple account credit reinstatements (attached logs)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking a look. We believe some of our dev teams accidentally created multiple trial accounts while onboarding between August 24–31. Each team used different emails but the same corporate billing card and a shared CI runner IP. We submitted a single appeal per account through the portal but haven’t heard back.

We attached appeal_logs.csv with 9 account IDs and the timestamps of each trial start. Can we get a one-time restore of the $500 trial credit to the primary billing account while we consolidate? We want to avoid interrupted integration tests.

Files attached: appeal_logs.csv (csv, 9 rows)

Appreciate any expedited help.

—Sara Nguyen
Ops lead, Hyperledger AI
ops@hyperledger.ai
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: multiple account credit reinstatements (attached logs) -- internal review needed

Forwarding Sara's appeal. External asked for a one-time restore across "primary billing account"; logs attached.

Quick asks:
- Neha: can you run the duplicate-account & payment-method overlap check (payment token hash + card last4) and flag any that match our abuse patterns?
- Rishi: please check IP / CI runner clusters for shared origins (especially 34.210.* / 18.194.* ranges) and signal if the traffic looks automated.
- Priyom: confirm whether a manual exception is allowed under current promo policy (Docs: promotions/credits_v2). If we allow, propose guardrails (single restore, TTL, account consolidation deadline).

Do not reply to the customer yet — I want consolidated findings. Mark urgency: high.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: multiple account credit reinstatements (attached logs) -- internal review results

Jordan / team,

Summary of checks done: attached account-mapping.pdf with a table of the 9 account IDs and our flags. Findings in brief:
- 6 of 9 accounts share the same payment token (same last4 & hashed token) — consistent with single org billing.
- 5 of 9 show creation from two closely-related IP ranges; traffic pattern (bursting during late-night CI runs) looks automated.
- One account shows a previous promo redemption that matches our known pattern for credit-cycling (trial + re-register).

Policy note: our promotions rules (credits_v2) disallow stacked trials across multiple accounts for the same billing instrument unless validated by TAM or Enterprise team. We should treat this as potential coordinated onboarding rather than fraud-as-malicious, but risk of abuse exists.

Recommendation:
- Reject blanket reinstatement for all accounts.
- Offer a single, manual $250 one-time credit to the primary billing account if Hyperledger signs a short mutual action plan: consolidate the listed accounts within 30 days and provide a named contact who will own consolidation. Credit will be issued after consolidation evidence is received.
- If Hyperledger declines, escalate to risk for potential promo-abuse rate-limiting on future sign-ups from the same payment token and IP ranges.

I attached account-mapping.pdf (pdf, 1 page) and exported the merged thread as support-thread-merge.eml for records.

Neha Kapoor
Risk & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <ops@hyperledger.ai>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: multiple account credit reinstatements (investigation & conditional offer)

Hi Sara — thanks for the details and the logs. Internal review shows overlapping payment tokens and CI-related IP bursts across multiple accounts. Because that pattern matches our promo stacking risk profile, we can’t do a blanket restore for all accounts.

That said, we want to keep onboarding smooth for partners. Proposed one-time resolution:
- Redwood will provision a single $250 one-time account credit to your primary billing account.
- Conditions: Hyperledger AI signs a short consolidation plan (I pasted a template link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-appeal-evidence) and confirms that the 9 accounts will be merged/closed within 30 days. Credit will be applied after we receive evidence of the consolidation start (e.g., admin contact + ticket ID).

If this is acceptable I’ll route the credit through Billing and tag as a manual promo exception (Deal DL-8942). If you’d prefer a full policy exception, we’ll need approval from Head of Revenue and a signed SOW covering incremental exposure.

Please confirm and provide the consolidation contact.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Hi Jordan — thank you, that solution works for us. We’ll appoint Priya Rao (priya@hyperledger.ai) as the consolidation owner and start the merge process this week. I’ve attached the signed one-page consolidation plan (sent via our secure doc system) and will send a ticket ID once the first account is closed.

We accept the $250 one-time credit and the 30-day consolidation timeline. Please advise next steps for Billing to apply the credit.

Best,
Sara
